text:
ria_k: heads up — we saw a spike of PCIe reset + Xid 13 bursts on two cards in us-west1 around 02:15 UTC. telemetry shows ~120 resets in 6m on node gpu-uw1-42

samir: ouch. did the node auto-cordon?

ops-bot: [alert] gpu-health: node=gpu-uw1-42 signal=xid13 burst=120 window=360s severity=warning

ria_k: it got a soft-taint from the health-prober but because of our current policy it didn't trigger an eviction — there were >3 long-running SLURM jobs so we held off.

jordan: is this the same pattern we saw last month before the full card swap? wondering if a hard evict would help or just cause churn.

matt-devops: proposal: introduce an eviction throttle + dedupe by card serial + per-region surge limiter. goal: avoid mass-drain when a noisy switch or infra blip causes many nodes to flicker.

anita: +1. can you sketch the rate-limiter rules? i want to review impact on capacity.

matt-devops: rough idea: maintain a token-bucket per-region and per-card-serial. token refill = 1 every 10m; bucket size = 3. only allow node eviction if bucket has token and node has >X low-prio tasks (configurable). also require corroboration from two independent signals (e.g., Xid burst AND ECC spike) within 5m.

ria_k: that helps avoid evicting because of a single transient Xid. also suggests we need a better pre-evict checklist: drain-preflight should run a quick health-run: memtest-lite + nv-checksum + kvcache-consistency probe. if preflight fails, proceed. if preflight passes but signal persists, escalate.

samir: how will this interact with Slurm drain? we can't leave SLURM jobs halfway. maybe we should prefer `scontrol requeue` for queued jobs and only preempt if slack-node has no running critical jobs.

matt-devops: agreed. decision matrix: if node.running_critical_jobs == true -> annotate and schedule maintenance window; if running_noncritical && tokens available -> graceful cordon + condefer-cancel preempt; else -> mark as monitor and escalate to oncall after 30m.

jordan: we should also simulate available capacity impact. suggestion: run a 24h chaos sim in staging with the limiter set to 1 token / 30m and bucket=2 and then measure failed job rate / queue latency.

ops-bot: [proposal] apply evict-throttle config to us-west1 staging: {"bucket_size":2, "refill_secs":1800, "corroboration_window_secs":300, "min_noncritical_jobs":1} (will not apply to prod)

ria_k: below is a draft config snippet for kube-drain-orch (RFC):

```yaml
name: evict-throttle-policy-v1
scope: region:us-west1
per_card_tokens: true
card_token_bucket:
  refill_seconds: 600
  capacity: 3
corroboration:
  required_signals: [xid_burst, ecc_rate]
  window_seconds: 300
preflight_checks:
  - memtest-lite
  - nv-health-check --quick
  - kvcache-check --read-verify
slurm_integration:
  drain_strategy: graceful_requeue
  max_wait_seconds: 1800
  preempt_noncritical: true

```

anita: nice. what's the alerting cadence? want to avoid pager fatigue if this happens again.

matt-devops: alerting plan: on first cordon -> ops-notify (non-pager). if 2 cords within 2h for same card-serial -> oncall pager. if >5 nodes in region cordoned within 30m -> major incident channel and auto-throttle region traffic (route new jobs to other region).

samir: cost angle — if we delay evictions to avoid churn, we might serve degraded performance and waste GPU cycles on retries; if we evict too fast we pay for replacements and increased job rescheduling. need to quantify. i'll run a quick cost vs. availability calc later today.

jordan: rollout plan?

ria_k: i can run the staging sim Jordan suggested and feed results to a short doc. Matt can PR policy to ops-config repo. plan: 1) staging sim 24h 2) review metrics 3) gated rollout to prod us-west1 with `bucket=1` 4) monitor 72h then expand.

matt-devops: i'll sketch the k8s operator changes to enforce per-card token buckets + require health-stack corroboration. will open PR and ping this thread.

ops-bot: [info] created ticket INFRA-4338: evict-throttle-policy + preflight checks (assignee=matt-devops)

anita: LGTM from SRE side. please include runbook steps for manual override (immediate evict, force-replace) and a rollback flag.

ria_k: thanks all. i'll attach the staging sim results and a small runbook once available. for now i'm marking node gpu-uw1-42 as under investigation and tagging it with `health:intermittent-reset`.

samir: thanks — feel free to @oncall if it starts repeating. :thumbsup:
